answer: In an agent marketplace, agents such as gale, sable, and nebula must each lock a $100 bond for 30 days before their bids count. The registry requires a separate deposit for every identity, so creating 1,000 eligible agents ties up $100,000 for a month. Randomly audited jobs with verifiable failures trigger bond forfeiture. Fake names remain cheap, but using them at scale requires capital and puts that capital at risk when agents cheat.
